10 /-!
11 # Path connectedness
12 
13 Continuing from `Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean`, this file defines path components and path-connected
14 spaces.
15 
16 ## Main definitions
17 
18 In the file the unit interval `[0, 1]` in `ℝ` is denoted by `I`, and `X` is a topological space.
19 
20 * `Joined (x y : X)` means there is a path between `x` and `y`.
21 * `Joined.somePath (h : Joined x y)` selects some path between two points `x` and `y`.
22 * `pathComponent (x : X)` is the set of points joined to `x`.
23 * `PathConnectedSpace X` is a predicate class asserting that `X` is non-empty and every two
24   points of `X` are joined.
25 
26 Then there are corresponding relative notions for `F : Set X`.
27 
28 * `JoinedIn F (x y : X)` means there is a path `γ` joining `x` to `y` with values in `F`.
29 * `JoinedIn.somePath (h : JoinedIn F x y)` selects a path from `x` to `y` inside `F`.
30 * `pathComponentIn F (x : X)` is the set of points joined to `x` in `F`.
31 * `IsPathConnected F` asserts that `F` is non-empty and every two
32   points of `F` are joined in `F`.
33 
34 ## Main theorems
35 
36 * `Joined` is an equivalence relation, while `JoinedIn F` is at least symmetric and transitive.
37 
38 One can link the absolute and relative version in two directions, using `(univ : Set X)` or the
39 subtype `↥F`.
40 
41 * `pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ : PathConnectedSpace X ↔ IsPathConnected (univ : Set X)`
42 * `isPathConnected_iff_pathConnectedSpace : IsPathConnected F ↔ PathConnectedSpace ↥F`
43 
44 Furthermore, it is shown that continuous images and quotients of path-connected sets/spaces are
45 path-connected, and that every path-connected set/space is also connected. (See
46 `Counterexamples.TopologistsSineCurve` for an example of a set in `ℝ × ℝ` that is connected but not
47 path-connected.)
48 -/
49 
50 @[expose] public section
51 
52 noncomputable section
53 
54 open Topology Filter unitInterval Set Function Pointwise Fin
55 
56 variable {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {x y z : X} {ι : Type*}
57 
58 /-! ### Being joined by a path -/
59 
60 
61 /-- The relation "being joined by a path". This is an equivalence relation. -/
62 def Joined (x y : X) : Prop :=
63   Nonempty (Path x y)
64 
65 @[refl]
66 theorem Joined.refl (x : X) : Joined x x :=
67   ⟨Path.refl x⟩
68 
69 /-- When two points are joined, choose some path from `x` to `y`. -/
70 def Joined.somePath (h : Joined x y) : Path x y :=
71   Nonempty.some h
72 
73 @[symm]
74 theorem Joined.symm {x y : X} (h : Joined x y) : Joined y x :=
75   ⟨h.somePath.symm⟩
76 
77 @[trans]
78 theorem Joined.trans {x y z : X} (hxy : Joined x y) (hyz : Joined y z) : Joined x z :=
79   ⟨hxy.somePath.trans hyz.somePath⟩
80 
81 @[to_additive]
82 theorem Joined.mul {M : Type*} [Mul M] [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousMul M]
83     {a b c d : M} (hs : Joined a b) (ht : Joined c d) : Joined (a * c) (b * d) :=
84   ⟨hs.somePath.mul ht.somePath⟩
85 
86 @[to_additive]
87 theorem Joined.listProd {M : Type*} [MulOneClass M] [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousMul M]
88     {l l' : List M} (h : List.Forall₂ Joined l l') :
89     Joined l.prod l'.prod := by
90   induction h with
91   | nil => rfl
92   | cons h₁ _ h₂ => exact h₁.mul h₂
93 
94 @[to_additive]
95 theorem Joined.inv {G : Type*} [Inv G] [TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousInv G]
96     {x y : G} (h : Joined x y) : Joined x⁻¹ y⁻¹ :=
97   ⟨h.somePath.inv⟩
98 
99 variable (X)
100 
101 /-- The setoid corresponding the equivalence relation of being joined by a continuous path. -/
102 @[implicit_reducible]
103 def pathSetoid : Setoid X where
104   r := Joined
105   iseqv := Equivalence.mk Joined.refl Joined.symm Joined.trans
106 
107 /-- The quotient type of points of a topological space modulo being joined by a continuous path. -/
108 def ZerothHomotopy :=
109   Quotient (pathSetoid X)
110 
111 /-- The quotient topology on path components. -/
112 instance : TopologicalSpace <| ZerothHomotopy X :=
113   inferInstanceAs <| TopologicalSpace <| Quotient _
114 
115 instance ZerothHomotopy.inhabited : Inhabited (ZerothHomotopy ℝ) :=
116   ⟨@Quotient.mk' ℝ (pathSetoid ℝ) 0⟩
117 
118 variable {X}
119 
120 /-! ### Being joined by a path inside a set -/
121 
122 
123 /-- The relation "being joined by a path in `F`". Not quite an equivalence relation since it's not
124 reflexive for points that do not belong to `F`. -/
125 def JoinedIn (F : Set X) (x y : X) : Prop :=
126   ∃ γ : Path x y, ∀ t, γ t ∈ F
127 
128 variable {F : Set X}
129 
130 theorem JoinedIn.mem (h : JoinedIn F x y) : x ∈ F ∧ y ∈ F := by
131   rcases h with ⟨γ, γ_in⟩
132   have : γ 0 ∈ F ∧ γ 1 ∈ F := by constructor <;> apply γ_in
133   simpa using this
134 
135 theorem JoinedIn.source_mem (h : JoinedIn F x y) : x ∈ F :=
136   h.mem.1
137 
138 theorem JoinedIn.target_mem (h : JoinedIn F x y) : y ∈ F :=
139   h.mem.2
140 
141 /-- When `x` and `y` are joined in `F`, choose a path from `x` to `y` inside `F` -/
142 def JoinedIn.somePath (h : JoinedIn F x y) : Path x y :=
143   Classical.choose h
144 
145 theorem JoinedIn.somePath_mem (h : JoinedIn F x y) (t : I) : h.somePath t ∈ F :=
146   Classical.choose_spec h t
147 
148 /-- If `x` and `y` are joined in the set `F`, then they are joined in the subtype `F`. -/
149 theorem JoinedIn.joined_subtype (h : JoinedIn F x y) :
150     Joined (⟨x, h.source_mem⟩ : F) (⟨y, h.target_mem⟩ : F) :=
151   ⟨{  toFun := fun t => ⟨h.somePath t, h.somePath_mem t⟩
152       continuous_toFun := by fun_prop
153       source' := by simp
154       target' := by simp }⟩
155 
156 theorem JoinedIn.ofLine {f : ℝ → X} (hf : ContinuousOn f I) (h₀ : f 0 = x) (h₁ : f 1 = y)
157     (hF : f '' I ⊆ F) : JoinedIn F x y :=
158   ⟨Path.ofLine hf h₀ h₁, fun t => hF <| Path.ofLine_mem hf h₀ h₁ t⟩
159 
160 theorem JoinedIn.joined (h : JoinedIn F x y) : Joined x y :=
161   ⟨h.somePath⟩
162 
163 theorem joinedIn_iff_joined (x_in : x ∈ F) (y_in : y ∈ F) :
164     JoinedIn F x y ↔ Joined (⟨x, x_in⟩ : F) (⟨y, y_in⟩ : F) :=
165   ⟨fun h => h.joined_subtype, fun h => ⟨h.somePath.map continuous_subtype_val, by simp⟩⟩
166 
167 @[simp]
168 theorem joinedIn_univ : JoinedIn univ x y ↔ Joined x y := by
169   simp [JoinedIn, Joined, exists_true_iff_nonempty]
170 
171 theorem JoinedIn.mono {U V : Set X} (h : JoinedIn U x y) (hUV : U ⊆ V) : JoinedIn V x y :=
172   ⟨h.somePath, fun t => hUV (h.somePath_mem t)⟩
173 
174 theorem JoinedIn.refl (h : x ∈ F) : JoinedIn F x x :=
175   ⟨Path.refl x, fun _t => h⟩
176 
177 @[symm]
178 theorem JoinedIn.symm (h : JoinedIn F x y) : JoinedIn F y x := by
179   obtain ⟨hx, hy⟩ := h.mem
180   simp_all only [joinedIn_iff_joined]
181   exact h.symm
182 
183 theorem JoinedIn.trans (hxy : JoinedIn F x y) (hyz : JoinedIn F y z) : JoinedIn F x z := by
184   obtain ⟨hx, hy⟩ := hxy.mem
185   obtain ⟨hx, hy⟩ := hyz.mem
186   simp_all only [joinedIn_iff_joined]
187   exact hxy.trans hyz
188 
189 theorem Specializes.joinedIn (h : x ⤳ y) (hx : x ∈ F) (hy : y ∈ F) : JoinedIn F x y := by
190   refine ⟨⟨⟨Set.piecewise {1} (const I y) (const I x), ?_⟩, by simp, by simp⟩, fun t ↦ ?_⟩
191   · exact isClosed_singleton.continuous_piecewise_of_specializes continuous_const continuous_const
192       fun _ ↦ h
193   · simp only [Path.coe_mk_mk, piecewise]
194     split_ifs <;> assumption
195 
196 theorem Inseparable.joinedIn (h : Inseparable x y) (hx : x ∈ F) (hy : y ∈ F) : JoinedIn F x y :=
197   h.specializes.joinedIn hx hy
198 
199 theorem JoinedIn.map_continuousOn (h : JoinedIn F x y) {f : X → Y} (hf : ContinuousOn f F) :
200     JoinedIn (f '' F) (f x) (f y) :=
201   let ⟨γ, hγ⟩ := h
202   ⟨γ.map' <| hf.mono (range_subset_iff.mpr hγ), fun t ↦ mem_image_of_mem _ (hγ t)⟩
203 
204 theorem JoinedIn.map (h : JoinedIn F x y) {f : X → Y} (hf : Continuous f) :
205     JoinedIn (f '' F) (f x) (f y) :=
206   h.map_continuousOn hf.continuousOn
207 
208 theorem Topology.IsInducing.joinedIn_image {f : X → Y} (hf : IsInducing f) (hx : x ∈ F)
209     (hy : y ∈ F) : JoinedIn (f '' F) (f x) (f y) ↔ JoinedIn F x y := by
210   refine ⟨?_, (.map · hf.continuous)⟩
211   rintro ⟨γ, hγ⟩
212   choose γ' hγ'F hγ' using hγ
213   have h₀ : x ⤳ γ' 0 := by rw [← hf.specializes_iff, hγ', γ.source]
214   have h₁ : γ' 1 ⤳ y := by rw [← hf.specializes_iff, hγ', γ.target]
215   have h : JoinedIn F (γ' 0) (γ' 1) := by
216     refine ⟨⟨⟨γ', ?_⟩, rfl, rfl⟩, hγ'F⟩
217     simpa only [hf.continuous_iff, comp_def, hγ'] using map_continuous γ
218   exact (h₀.joinedIn hx (hγ'F _)).trans <| h.trans <| h₁.joinedIn (hγ'F _) hy
219 
220 @[to_additive]
221 theorem JoinedIn.mul {M : Type*} [Mul M] [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousMul M]
222     {s t : Set M} {a b c d : M} (hs : JoinedIn s a b) (ht : JoinedIn t c d) :
223     JoinedIn (s * t) (a * c) (b * d) :=
224   ⟨hs.somePath.mul ht.somePath, fun t ↦ Set.mul_mem_mul (hs.somePath_mem t) (ht.somePath_mem t)⟩
225 
226 @[to_additive]
227 theorem JoinedIn.inv {G : Type*} [InvolutiveInv G] [TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousInv G]
228     {s : Set G} {a b : G} (hs : JoinedIn s a b) :
229     JoinedIn s⁻¹ a⁻¹ b⁻¹ :=
230   ⟨hs.somePath.inv, fun t ↦ Set.inv_mem_inv.mpr (hs.somePath_mem t)⟩
231 
232 /-! ### Path component -/
233 
234 /-- The path component of `x` is the set of points that can be joined to `x`. -/
235 def pathComponent (x : X) :=
236   { y | Joined x y }
237 
238 theorem mem_pathComponent_iff : x ∈ pathComponent y ↔ Joined y x := .rfl
239 
240 @[simp]
241 theorem mem_pathComponent_self (x : X) : x ∈ pathComponent x :=
242   Joined.refl x
243 
244 @[simp]
245 theorem pathComponent.nonempty (x : X) : (pathComponent x).Nonempty :=
246   ⟨x, mem_pathComponent_self x⟩
247 
248 theorem mem_pathComponent_of_mem (h : x ∈ pathComponent y) : y ∈ pathComponent x :=
249   Joined.symm h
250 
251 theorem pathComponent_symm : x ∈ pathComponent y ↔ y ∈ pathComponent x :=
252   ⟨fun h => mem_pathComponent_of_mem h, fun h => mem_pathComponent_of_mem h⟩
253 
254 theorem pathComponent_congr (h : x ∈ pathComponent y) : pathComponent x = pathComponent y := by
255   ext z
256   constructor
257   · intro h'
258     rw [pathComponent_symm]
259     exact (h.trans h').symm
260   · intro h'
261     rw [pathComponent_symm] at h' ⊢
262     exact h'.trans h
263 
264 theorem pathComponent_subset_component (x : X) : pathComponent x ⊆ connectedComponent x :=
265   fun y h =>
266   (isConnected_range h.somePath.continuous).subset_connectedComponent ⟨0, by simp⟩ ⟨1, by simp⟩
267 
268 /-- Every connected component is a union of path connected components -/
269 theorem biUnion_connectedComponent_pathComponent_eq (x : X) :
270     (⋃ y ∈ connectedComponent x, pathComponent y) = connectedComponent x := by
271   simp only [Set.ext_iff, mem_iUnion₂]
272   exact fun z ↦ ⟨fun ⟨y, hy, hz⟩ ↦ connectedComponent_eq hy ▸ pathComponent_subset_component _ hz,
273     (⟨z, ·, mem_pathComponent_self z⟩)⟩
274 
275 /-- The canonical map which sends a path component of `X` (as a term of `ZerothHomotopy X`) to the
276 connected component containing it (as a term of `ConnectedComponents X`). -/
277 def ZerothHomotopy.toConnectedComponents : ZerothHomotopy X → ConnectedComponents X :=
278   Quotient.map id fun x _ h ↦ connectedComponent_eq <| pathComponent_subset_component x h
279 
280 @[simp]
281 theorem ZerothHomotopy.toConnectedComponents_apply (x : X) : toConnectedComponents ⟦x⟧ = ⟦x⟧ :=
282   rfl
283 
284 /-- There are at least as many path connected components as there are connected components -/
285 theorem ZerothHomotopy.toConnectedComponents_surjective :
286     toConnectedComponents (X := X) |>.Surjective :=
287   Quotient.map_surjective _ surjective_id
288 
289 /-- The path component of `x` in `F` is the set of points that can be joined to `x` in `F`. -/
290 def pathComponentIn (F : Set X) (x : X) :=
291   { y | JoinedIn F x y }
292 
293 @[simp]
294 theorem pathComponentIn_univ (x : X) : pathComponentIn univ x = pathComponent x := by
295   simp [pathComponentIn, pathComponent, JoinedIn, Joined, exists_true_iff_nonempty]
296 
297 theorem Joined.mem_pathComponent (hyz : Joined y z) (hxy : y ∈ pathComponent x) :
298     z ∈ pathComponent x :=
299   hxy.trans hyz
300 
301 theorem mem_pathComponentIn_self (h : x ∈ F) : x ∈ pathComponentIn F x :=
302   JoinedIn.refl h
303 
304 theorem pathComponentIn_subset : pathComponentIn F x ⊆ F :=
305   fun _ hy ↦ hy.target_mem
306 
307 theorem pathComponentIn_nonempty_iff : (pathComponentIn F x).Nonempty ↔ x ∈ F :=
308   ⟨fun ⟨_, ⟨γ, hγ⟩⟩ ↦ γ.source ▸ hγ 0, fun hx ↦ ⟨x, mem_pathComponentIn_self hx⟩⟩
309 
310 theorem pathComponentIn_congr (h : x ∈ pathComponentIn F y) :
311     pathComponentIn F x = pathComponentIn F y := by
312   ext; exact ⟨h.trans, h.symm.trans⟩
313 
314 @[gcongr]
315 theorem pathComponentIn_mono {G : Set X} (h : F ⊆ G) :
316     pathComponentIn F x ⊆ pathComponentIn G x :=
317   fun _ ⟨γ, hγ⟩ ↦ ⟨γ, fun t ↦ h (hγ t)⟩
318 
319 /-! ### Path component of the identity in a group -/
320 
321 /-- The path component of the identity in a topological monoid, as a submonoid. -/
322 @[to_additive (attr := simps) /-- The path component of the identity in an additive topological
323 monoid, as an additive submonoid. -/]
324 def Submonoid.pathComponentOne (M : Type*) [Monoid M] [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousMul M] :
325     Submonoid M where
326   carrier := pathComponent (1 : M)
327   mul_mem' {m₁ m₂} hm₁ hm₂ := by simpa using hm₁.mul hm₂
328   one_mem' := mem_pathComponent_self 1
329 
330 /-- The path component of the identity in a topological group, as a subgroup. -/
331 @[to_additive (attr := simps!) /-- The path component of the identity in an additive topological
332 group, as an additive subgroup. -/]
333 def Subgroup.pathComponentOne (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
334     Subgroup G where
335   toSubmonoid := .pathComponentOne G
336   inv_mem' {g} hg := by simpa using hg.inv
337 
338 /-- The path component of the identity in a topological group is normal. -/
339 @[to_additive]
340 instance Subgroup.Normal.pathComponentOne (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
341     [IsTopologicalGroup G] : (Subgroup.pathComponentOne G).Normal where
342   conj_mem _ := fun ⟨γ⟩ g ↦ ⟨⟨⟨(g * γ · * g⁻¹), by fun_prop⟩, by simp, by simp⟩⟩
343 
344 /-! ### Path connected sets -/
345 
346 
347 /-- A set `F` is path connected if it contains a point that can be joined to all other in `F`. -/
348 def IsPathConnected (F : Set X) : Prop :=
349   ∃ x ∈ F, ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ F → JoinedIn F x y
350 
351 theorem isPathConnected_iff_eq : IsPathConnected F ↔ ∃ x ∈ F, pathComponentIn F x = F := by
352   constructor <;> rintro ⟨x, x_in, h⟩ <;> use x, x_in
353   · ext y
354     exact ⟨fun hy => hy.mem.2, @h _⟩
355   · intro y y_in
356     rwa [← h] at y_in
357 
358 theorem IsPathConnected.joinedIn (h : IsPathConnected F) :
359     ∀ᵉ (x ∈ F) (y ∈ F), JoinedIn F x y := fun _x x_in _y y_in =>
360   let ⟨_b, _b_in, hb⟩ := h
361   (hb x_in).symm.trans (hb y_in)
362 
363 theorem isPathConnected_iff :
364     IsPathConnected F ↔ F.Nonempty ∧ ∀ᵉ (x ∈ F) (y ∈ F), JoinedIn F x y :=
365   ⟨fun h =>
366     ⟨let ⟨b, b_in, _hb⟩ := h; ⟨b, b_in⟩, h.joinedIn⟩,
367     fun ⟨⟨b, b_in⟩, h⟩ => ⟨b, b_in, h _ b_in⟩⟩
368 
369 theorem IsPathConnected.nonempty (h : IsPathConnected F) : F.Nonempty :=
370   isPathConnected_iff.mp h |>.1
371 
372 /-- If `f` is continuous on `F` and `F` is path-connected, so is `f(F)`. -/
373 theorem IsPathConnected.image' (hF : IsPathConnected F)
374     {f : X → Y} (hf : ContinuousOn f F) : IsPathConnected (f '' F) := by
375   rcases hF with ⟨x, x_in, hx⟩
376   use f x, mem_image_of_mem f x_in
377   rintro _ ⟨y, y_in, rfl⟩
378   refine ⟨(hx y_in).somePath.map' ?_, fun t ↦ ⟨_, (hx y_in).somePath_mem t, rfl⟩⟩
379   exact hf.mono (range_subset_iff.2 (hx y_in).somePath_mem)
380 
381 /-- If `f` is continuous and `F` is path-connected, so is `f(F)`. -/
382 theorem IsPathConnected.image (hF : IsPathConnected F) {f : X → Y} (hf : Continuous f) :
383     IsPathConnected (f '' F) :=
384   hF.image' hf.continuousOn
385 
386 @[to_additive]
387 theorem IsPathConnected.mul {M : Type*} [Mul M] [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousMul M]
388     {s t : Set M} (hs : IsPathConnected s) (ht : IsPathConnected t) :
389     IsPathConnected (s * t) :=
390   let ⟨a, ha_mem, ha⟩ := hs; let ⟨b, hb_mem, hb⟩ := ht
391   ⟨a * b, mul_mem_mul ha_mem hb_mem, Set.forall_mem_image2.2 fun _x hx _y hy ↦ (ha hx).mul (hb hy)⟩
392 
393 @[to_additive]
394 theorem IsPathConnected.inv {G : Type*} [InvolutiveInv G] [TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousInv G]
395     {s : Set G} (hs : IsPathConnected s) :
396     IsPathConnected s⁻¹ :=
397   let ⟨a, ha_mem, ha⟩ := hs
398   ⟨a⁻¹, inv_mem_inv.mpr ha_mem, fun x hx ↦ by simpa using ha (mem_inv.mp hx) |>.map continuous_inv⟩
399 
400 /-- If `f : X → Y` is an inducing map, `f(F)` is path-connected iff `F` is. -/
401 nonrec theorem Topology.IsInducing.isPathConnected_iff {f : X → Y} (hf : IsInducing f) :
402     IsPathConnected F ↔ IsPathConnected (f '' F) := by
403   simp only [IsPathConnected, forall_mem_image, exists_mem_image]
404   refine exists_congr fun x ↦ and_congr_right fun hx ↦ forall₂_congr fun y hy ↦ ?_
405   rw [hf.joinedIn_image hx hy]
406 
407 /-- If `h : X → Y` is a homeomorphism, `h(s)` is path-connected iff `s` is. -/
408 @[simp]
409 theorem Homeomorph.isPathConnected_image {s : Set X} (h : X ≃ₜ Y) :
410     IsPathConnected (h '' s) ↔ IsPathConnected s :=
411   h.isInducing.isPathConnected_iff.symm
412 
413 /-- If `h : X → Y` is a homeomorphism, `h⁻¹(s)` is path-connected iff `s` is. -/
414 @[simp]
415 theorem Homeomorph.isPathConnected_preimage {s : Set Y} (h : X ≃ₜ Y) :
416     IsPathConnected (h ⁻¹' s) ↔ IsPathConnected s := by
417   rw [← Homeomorph.image_symm]; exact h.symm.isPathConnected_image
418 
419 theorem IsPathConnected.mem_pathComponent (h : IsPathConnected F) (x_in : x ∈ F) (y_in : y ∈ F) :
420     y ∈ pathComponent x :=
421   (h.joinedIn x x_in y y_in).joined
422 
423 theorem IsPathConnected.subset_pathComponent (h : IsPathConnected F) (x_in : x ∈ F) :
424     F ⊆ pathComponent x := fun _y y_in => h.mem_pathComponent x_in y_in
425 
426 theorem IsPathConnected.subset_pathComponentIn {s : Set X} (hs : IsPathConnected s)
427     (hxs : x ∈ s) (hsF : s ⊆ F) : s ⊆ pathComponentIn F x :=
428   fun y hys ↦ (hs.joinedIn x hxs y hys).mono hsF
429 
430 theorem isPathConnected_singleton (x : X) : IsPathConnected ({x} : Set X) := by
431   refine ⟨x, rfl, ?_⟩
432   rintro y rfl
433   exact JoinedIn.refl rfl
434 
435 theorem isPathConnected_pathComponentIn (h : x ∈ F) : IsPathConnected (pathComponentIn F x) :=
436   ⟨x, mem_pathComponentIn_self h, fun _ ⟨γ, hγ⟩ ↦ by
437     refine ⟨γ, fun t ↦
438       ⟨(γ.truncateOfLE t.2.1).cast (γ.extend_zero.symm) (γ.extend_extends' t).symm, fun t' ↦ ?_⟩⟩
439     dsimp [Path.truncateOfLE, Path.truncate]
440     exact γ.extend_extends' ⟨min (max t'.1 0) t.1, by simp [t.2.1, t.2.2]⟩ ▸ hγ _⟩
441 
442 theorem isPathConnected_pathComponent : IsPathConnected (pathComponent x) := by
443   rw [← pathComponentIn_univ]
444   exact isPathConnected_pathComponentIn (mem_univ x)
445 
446 theorem IsPathConnected.union {U V : Set X} (hU : IsPathConnected U) (hV : IsPathConnected V)
447     (hUV : (U ∩ V).Nonempty) : IsPathConnected (U ∪ V) := by
448   rcases hUV with ⟨x, xU, xV⟩
449   use x, Or.inl xU
450   rintro y (yU | yV)
451   · exact (hU.joinedIn x xU y yU).mono subset_union_left
452   · exact (hV.joinedIn x xV y yV).mono subset_union_right
453 
454 /-- If a set `W` is path-connected, then it is also path-connected when seen as a set in a smaller
455 ambient type `U` (when `U` contains `W`). -/
456 theorem IsPathConnected.preimage_coe {U W : Set X} (hW : IsPathConnected W) (hWU : W ⊆ U) :
457     IsPathConnected (((↑) : U → X) ⁻¹' W) := by
458   rwa [IsInducing.subtypeVal.isPathConnected_iff, Subtype.image_preimage_val, inter_eq_right.2 hWU]
459 
460 set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
461 theorem IsPathConnected.exists_path_through_family {n : ℕ}
462     {s : Set X} (h : IsPathConnected s) (p : Fin (n + 1) → X) (hp : ∀ i, p i ∈ s) :
463     ∃ γ : Path (p 0) (p (last n)), range γ ⊆ s ∧ ∀ i, p i ∈ range γ := by
464   cases p using snocCases with | _ p x => ?_
465   simp only [forall_fin_succ', snoc_castSucc, snoc_last, Path.cast_coe,
466     Path.target_mem_range, and_true] at hp ⊢
467   obtain ⟨hp, hx⟩ := hp
468   induction p using snocInduction generalizing x with
469   | elim0 =>
470     simp only [snoc_zero]
471     use Path.refl x
472     simp [hx]
473   | @snoc n p y hp₂ =>
474     simp only [forall_fin_succ', snoc_castSucc, snoc_last, snoc_apply_zero, Path.cast_coe] at hp ⊢
475     obtain ⟨hp, hy⟩ := hp
476     specialize hp₂ y hp hy
477     obtain ⟨γ₀, hγ₀s, hγ₀p⟩ := hp₂
478     obtain ⟨γ₁, hγ₁⟩ := h.joinedIn y hy x hx
479     rw [← range_subset_iff] at hγ₁
480     use γ₀.trans γ₁
481     simp only [Path.trans_range, mem_union, Path.source_mem_range, or_true, and_true,
482       union_subset_iff]
483     tauto
484 
485 theorem IsPathConnected.exists_path_through_family' {n : ℕ}
486     {s : Set X} (h : IsPathConnected s) (p : Fin (n + 1) → X) (hp : ∀ i, p i ∈ s) :
487     ∃ (γ : Path (p 0) (p (last n))) (t : Fin (n + 1) → I), (∀ t, γ t ∈ s) ∧ ∀ i, γ (t i) = p i := by
488   rcases h.exists_path_through_family p hp with ⟨γ, hγ⟩
489   rcases hγ with ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
490   simp only [range, mem_setOf_eq] at h₂
491   rw [range_subset_iff] at h₁
492   choose! t ht using h₂
493   exact ⟨γ, t, h₁, ht⟩
494 
495 /-! ### Path connected spaces -/
496 
497 
498 /-- A topological space is path-connected if it is non-empty and every two points can be
499 joined by a continuous path. -/
500 @[mk_iff]
501 class PathConnectedSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
502   /-- A path-connected space must be nonempty. -/
503   nonempty : Nonempty X
504   /-- Any two points in a path-connected space must be joined by a continuous path. -/
505   joined : ∀ x y : X, Joined x y
506 
507 theorem pathConnectedSpace_iff_zerothHomotopy :
508     PathConnectedSpace X ↔ Nonempty (ZerothHomotopy X) ∧ Subsingleton (ZerothHomotopy X) := by
509   letI := pathSetoid X
510   constructor
511   · intro h
512     refine ⟨(nonempty_quotient_iff _).mpr h.1, ⟨?_⟩⟩
513     rintro ⟨x⟩ ⟨y⟩
514     exact Quotient.sound (PathConnectedSpace.joined x y)
515   · unfold ZerothHomotopy
516     rintro ⟨h, h'⟩
517     exact ⟨(nonempty_quotient_iff _).mp h, fun x y => Quotient.exact <| Subsingleton.elim ⟦x⟧ ⟦y⟧⟩
518 
519 namespace PathConnectedSpace
520 
521 variable [PathConnectedSpace X]
522 
523 /-- Use path-connectedness to build a path between two points. -/
524 def somePath (x y : X) : Path x y :=
525   Nonempty.some (joined x y)
526 
527 end PathConnectedSpace
528 
529 theorem pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ : PathConnectedSpace X ↔ IsPathConnected (univ : Set X) := by
530   simp [pathConnectedSpace_iff, isPathConnected_iff, nonempty_iff_univ_nonempty]
531 
532 theorem isPathConnected_iff_pathConnectedSpace : IsPathConnected F ↔ PathConnectedSpace F := by
533   rw [pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ, IsInducing.subtypeVal.isPathConnected_iff, image_univ,
534     Subtype.range_val_subtype, setOf_mem_eq]
535 
536 theorem isPathConnected_univ [PathConnectedSpace X] : IsPathConnected (univ : Set X) :=
537   pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ.mp inferInstance
538 
539 theorem isPathConnected_range [PathConnectedSpace X] {f : X → Y} (hf : Continuous f) :
540     IsPathConnected (range f) := by
541   rw [← image_univ]
542   exact isPathConnected_univ.image hf
543 
544 theorem Function.Surjective.pathConnectedSpace [PathConnectedSpace X]
545     {f : X → Y} (hf : Surjective f) (hf' : Continuous f) : PathConnectedSpace Y := by
546   rw [pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ, ← hf.range_eq]
547   exact isPathConnected_range hf'
548 
549 instance Quotient.instPathConnectedSpace {s : Setoid X} [PathConnectedSpace X] :
550     PathConnectedSpace (Quotient s) :=
551   Quotient.mk'_surjective.pathConnectedSpace continuous_coinduced_rng
552 
553 /-- This is a special case of `NormedSpace.instPathConnectedSpace` (and
554 `IsTopologicalAddGroup.pathConnectedSpace`). It exists only to simplify dependencies. -/
555 instance Real.instPathConnectedSpace : PathConnectedSpace ℝ where
556   joined x y := ⟨⟨⟨fun (t : I) ↦ (1 - t) * x + t * y, by fun_prop⟩, by simp, by simp⟩⟩
557   nonempty := inferInstance
558 
559 theorem pathConnectedSpace_iff_eq : PathConnectedSpace X ↔ ∃ x : X, pathComponent x = univ := by
560   simp [pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ, isPathConnected_iff_eq]
561 
562 -- see Note [lower instance priority]
563 instance (priority := 100) PathConnectedSpace.connectedSpace [PathConnectedSpace X] :
564     ConnectedSpace X := by
565   rw [connectedSpace_iff_connectedComponent]
566   rcases isPathConnected_iff_eq.mp (pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ.mp ‹_›) with ⟨x, _x_in, hx⟩
567   use x
568   rw [← univ_subset_iff]
569   exact (by simpa using hx : pathComponent x = univ) ▸ pathComponent_subset_component x
570 
571 /-- A path-connected set is connected.
572 
573 (See `Counterexamples.TopologistsSineCurve` for the standard counterexample showing that the
574 converse is false.) -/
575 theorem IsPathConnected.isConnected (hF : IsPathConnected F) : IsConnected F := by
576   rw [isConnected_iff_connectedSpace]
577   rw [isPathConnected_iff_pathConnectedSpace] at hF
578   exact @PathConnectedSpace.connectedSpace _ _ hF
579 
580 namespace PathConnectedSpace
581 
582 variable [PathConnectedSpace X]
583 
584 theorem exists_path_through_family {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 1) → X) :
585     ∃ γ : Path (p 0) (p (last n)), ∀ i, p i ∈ range γ := by
586   have : IsPathConnected (univ : Set X) := pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ.mp (by infer_instance)
587   rcases this.exists_path_through_family p fun _i => True.intro with ⟨γ, -, h⟩
588   exact ⟨γ, h⟩
589 
590 theorem exists_path_through_family' {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 1) → X) :
591     ∃ (γ : Path (p 0) (p (last n))) (t : Fin (n + 1) → I), ∀ i, γ (t i) = p i := by
592   have : IsPathConnected (univ : Set X) := pathConnectedSpace_iff_univ.mp (by infer_instance)
593   rcases this.exists_path_through_family' p fun _i => True.intro with ⟨γ, t, -, h⟩
594   exact ⟨γ, t, h⟩
595 
596 end PathConnectedSpace
597 
598 /-- The preimage of a singleton in `ZerothHomotopy` is the path component of an element in the
599 equivalence class. -/
600 theorem ZerothHomotopy.preimage_singleton_eq_pathComponent (x : X) :
601     Quotient.mk' (s := pathSetoid X) ⁻¹' {⟦x⟧} = pathComponent x := by
602   ext y
603   rw [mem_preimage, mem_singleton_iff, eq_comm, mem_pathComponent_iff]
604   exact Quotient.eq
605 
606 instance [CompactSpace X] : CompactSpace <| ZerothHomotopy X := Quotient.compactSpace
